title: Footsteps Return — Seven Topological Realms
composerCredit: Original score composed for Topology Gomoku
copyright: Original project score; no third-party composition

sourceMusic.declaration: Every pitched and rhythmic event is original to this project. No reference-PV music was imported, traced, transcribed, or transformed.

motif.name: returning-footsteps cell
motif.dramaturgy: The five-note cell is heard as a compact prologue signal, not an arpeggio and not a melody forced through all seven chapters. Chapter cohesion comes from a short D/A hinge sonority instead.

boundarySonority.use: A brief timbral relay at structural hinges only; never expanded into a shared chapter theme.

arc: piano states a clear independent theme
transparent strings refract it without doubling
restrained bass clarinet and piano close on a bright suspended D
rounded bass clarinet opens the orbit
pizzicato strings and cyclic percussion accelerate lateral travel
the cello reaches stage right while the clarinet rounds back into the hinge
piano cycle begins alone
celesta enters on an offset period while strings mark intersections
both motives shorten and interlock into one meshed lattice
viola traces an asymmetrical folded line
bass clarinet appears on the apparent reverse side
reverse-bow string envelopes compress the two directions into one surface
high and low ensembles trade a jagged signal
metallic punctuation shortens the antiphonal distance
both registers collide in a propelled D/E-flat hinge
celesta draws a cold oblique figure
divided strings mirror it around a chamber-choir plane
glass and voices converge without warming the harmony
piano and horn open the horizon
full strings and winds broaden the melody while choir enters above speech
the orchestra reaches a bright crest and releases forward into the gallery

joins.pivot: D/A harmonics become the piano pickup
A/D piano resonance rounds into B-flat clarinet
rightmost pizzicato C/G becomes a high celesta intersection
celesta F-sharp/C-sharp folds into octatonic viola C/F-sharp
viola D/A is struck into metallic D/E-flat propulsion
metallic E/B overtone becomes cold celesta E/B
choir D/A plane acquires a bright horn F-sharp
violin D/A crest breaks into a celesta mosaic
gallery A/E relay becomes the final D-major anacrusis

form.identity: A compact, unevenly accented D–F–G–A–C signal appears in piano against buoyant bass harmonics and celesta air; it is a prologue emblem, not the chapter melody.
form.narrationStrategy: Short attacks and open fifths leave the speech presence band unfilled.
form.resolution: A brief D/A harmonic crosses the cut while Plane's piano pickup enters.

form.identity: An independent D-Lydian piano theme with a clear hook, translucent string refractions and restrained upper bass clarinet.
form.narrationStrategy: Piano phrases answer sentence gaps; strings avoid continuous midrange doubling.
form.resolution: The piano sustains a bright D/A relay while Cylinder's rounded clarinet pickup arrives early.

form.identity: B-flat-Mixolydian bass clarinet curves over one-direction cello pizzicato, viola offbeats and a 3+3 percussion orbit that travels left to right.
form.narrationStrategy: Detached strings and rounded wind notes preserve consonant clarity.
form.resolution: The final rightward pizzicato overlaps a high Torus celesta intersection.

form.identity: Piano and celesta carry two unrelated motives on 4.75- and 5.25-second periods, gradually shortening until their attacks mesh.
form.narrationStrategy: The two keyboards alternate register and do not accumulate a continuous pad.
form.resolution: The meshed celesta F-sharp/C-sharp remains sounding as Möbius viola enters below it.

form.identity: A C-octatonic viola line in 3+2+3/8 folds around bass clarinet responses and reverse-envelope string textures; mysterious, alert and unsentimental.
form.narrationStrategy: Lead and response trade the center register; reverse-bow colours stay soft and high.
form.resolution: Viola D/A crosses into a metallic Klein pickup without a silent seam.

form.identity: D-Phrygian-dominant high and low ensembles trade jagged 6/8 calls, metallic strikes and increasingly compressed register jumps.
form.narrationStrategy: High and low blocks alternate rather than stack beneath narration.
form.resolution: The last metal E/B overtone becomes Projective's celesta attack before the cut.

form.identity: An E-Lydian celesta figure and its oblique string mirror hover around chamber choir and glass-like percussion in a cold transcendent plane.
form.narrationStrategy: Choir is vowel-only and pianissimo; celesta attacks are discrete, never a constant shimmer.
form.resolution: A D/A choir plane remains while Sphere horn adds F-sharp and opens the horizon.

form.identity: A new broad D-major melody grows from piano and horn through full strings, bass clarinet, restrained percussion and choir to a bright orchestral crest.
form.density: broad accumulating orchestra with breathing gaps
form.narrationStrategy: The full ensemble enters in layers; sustained inner parts thin during sentence centers.
form.resolution: The crest hands D/A from violin to gallery celesta instead of closing by fade.

form.identity: Short, recognizably different timbral fragments pass through the ensemble as one forward-moving mosaic.
form.narrationStrategy: The first seven seconds are narration-free; texture narrows before outro speech.
form.resolution: A/E strings overlap the final piano anacrusis.

form.identity: Piano, horn and choir turn the accumulated energy into a warm D-major closing paragraph rather than returning to the mournful rejected theme.
form.narrationStrategy: Melodic attacks fall between phrase centers and the final chord begins after the last spoken emphasis.
form.resolution: A D6/9 chord starts at 177.2 seconds and decays naturally to 180.3.

form.identity: The bright D6/9 tail survives the logo entrance; the last 3.052 seconds carry deliberate final silence.
form.narrationStrategy: No new attack and no added noise floor.
form.resolution: Natural decay, then silence; no hard fade truncates the cadence.

parts.name: Piano
parts.role: Plane lead, Torus first cycle, Sphere melody and final cadence

parts.name: Celesta
parts.role: Torus second cycle, Projective lead and timbral relay

parts.name: Violin I
parts.role: Klein high calls, Projective mirror and Sphere crest

parts.name: Violin II
parts.role: transparent refraction, reverse-bow colour and divided strings

parts.name: Viola
parts.role: Möbius lead, Cylinder offbeat and inner orchestral motion

parts.name: Cello
parts.role: Cylinder travelling pizzicato, Klein low reply and Sphere foundation

parts.name: Double Bass
parts.role: buoyant harmonics, propulsion and cadence weight

parts.name: French Horn
parts.role: structural warmth and broad Sphere lead

parts.name: Bass Clarinet
parts.role: rounded Cylinder lead, Möbius reverse side and Klein low calls

parts.name: Choir Aahs
parts.role: weak Projective plane and bright Sphere/outro halo

parts.name: Restrained Percussion
parts.role: cyclic wood/metal pulse and controlled structural punctuation

render.spatialization: MuseScore renders every stem; score-audio.mjs applies declared equal-power stereo positions and Cylinder automation to those real PCM stems before the final stem sum.
render.tailPolicy: Score events end at 180.300. MusicXML uses an import-safe 1/32-note grid through 183.250; rendered files add 102 ms of silence and are trimmed to the measured 183.352-second master without fading an unresolved phrase.
render.normalization: FFmpeg converts MuseScore output to 48 kHz stereo PCM, sums spatialized stems, and applies a transparent -1 dBFS safety limiter only if needed.
